subject: Model slate & hourly load profile — ArborPay onboarding
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@arborpay.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ArborPay onboarding — context & throughput baseline

Connor — thanks again for the demo today. Two quick asks to help our engineering team size the integration:

1) Candidate model shortlist (we need sensible tradeoffs: latency-sensitive endpoints vs long-document reconciliation).
2) Recommended context window minima — we expect a mix of short (single-turn) and long (multi-document) workflows; want to understand if 8k is enough or we should plan for 32k/64k.
3) Ballpark token volumes: our product team estimates ~1.8M API calls/month initially (ramp to ~6M), average user exchange ~850 tokens (prompt+completion), with daily peak traffic concentrated in US business hours. We need hourly peaks for Dedicated sizing and any guidance on batching/caching that materially changes capacity.

Can you and your team put together a concise model + hourly load profile we can hand to our infra lead? The integrations team would like this by early next week.

—Samir
Samir Desai
Head of Integrations | ArborPay
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Samir Desai <samir@arborpay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ArborPay onboarding — context & throughput baseline

Samir — thanks for the concrete numbers, that helps a lot. I sketched an initial model slate and an hourly profile to hand to your infra team; attaching an XLSX with assumptions and a CSV with the shortlist. High level summary below — Ben and Monica, tagging you for technical sizing and the customer success handoff respectively.

High-level recommendations (short):
- Short/latency-sensitive: redwood-7b-latency (8k) — good compromise for low P95 and cost.
- Mixed / standard: redwood-13b-optimized (16k–32k) — better quality for multi-turn flows; suggest 16k initially, choose 32k if reconciliation docs are frequently concatenated.
- Long-context reconciliation: redwood-34b-window (32k) or redwood-34b-extended (64k) — only enable for specific reconciliation routes to limit cost.

Sizing notes (from your numbers):
- Baseline traffic: 1.8M calls/month => ~1.5M tokens/hour baseline (assumes 850 tokens/call and smoothing).
- Ramp target: 6M calls/month => ~5.0M tokens/hour at peak daytime window.
- Peak hourly QPS: planning for 6–8 RPS sustained during peak minutes; burst to 25 RPS for short spikes in payment events.

Attached: ArborPay_workload_estimate_v1.xlsx and model_shortlist.csv. Ben — can you review the perf assumptions (batching, expected cache hit, pod counts) and confirm whether Dedicated vs Hosted Dedicated reservations make sense here? Monica — I'll book a 1-hour kickoff with ArborPay once we align on the shortlist and MAP.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Samir Desai <samir@arborpay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ArborPay onboarding — context & throughput baseline

Agree with Connor's slate; a few technical clarifications and explicit numbers so infra can size nodes: 

Model choices and why: 
- redwood-7b-latency (8k): 8k context, quantized path (int8) — P95 latency ~120–200ms on A10-equivalent for single-threaded low-batch; good for token-limited endpoints (fraud-check quick).
- redwood-13b-optimized (16k): balance of quality and throughput; use as default for conversational routes where context stacking occurs.
- redwood-34b-window (32k): for reconciliation routes that need full invoice history; enable only on a small subset of endpoints to limit cost.

Batching & cache assumptions (affects pod counts):
- Continuous batching window: 8–12ms for latency-sensitive endpoints; 25–40ms for lower-priority reconciliation flows.
- KV/prefix caching: expect ~10–18% hit rate on repeated prompts (session-based caching) — conservatively use 12% hit for capacity planning.
- Token mix: we used 450 prompt tokens / 400 completion tokens average => 850 tokens/call. If ArborPay can trim prompts via summarization/prettifying, that reduces tokens/call materially.

Pod/socket sizing (rough; for planning only):
- Baseline (1.8M calls/mo): plan for 2 dedicated GPU pods (A10x2 equivalent) to meet latency SLOs with small autoscale headroom.
- Peak (ramp to 6M calls/mo & peak bursts): autoscale up to 8 pods across two availability zones. For the 32k model, allocate separate pool with 2 dedicated 34b-class pods (hot-standby can be used with cold-start fallback).
- Batching policy: set max batch tokens to 12k and per-request limit to 2k to keep tail latency reasonable.

Hourly token estimates (concrete):
- Baseline: 1.8M calls/month => ~1,080,000 tokens/hour (24h smoothing) — our XLSX uses 1.1M as a conservative baseline.
- Daytime peak window (US business hours, 9h): concentrated traffic pushes peak to ~4.8M tokens/hour.
- Burst minutes: short bursts can reach ~12M tokens/hour equivalent if many payment events fire; autoscaling + throttling recommended.

Ops cautions:
- Route long-context reconciliation through a separate path with soft quota and explicit cost controls (canary with logging + QoS).
- Consider early prefix-summarization to reduce required context; Redwood Optimize can supply sample prompt adapters.

Attaching model_shortlist.csv with perf numbers and rough cost multipliers. Happy to jump on a quick call with ArborPay infra to walk these through.

—Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: model_shortlist.csv]
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: ArborPay onboarding — context & throughput baseline

Thanks everyone — summary and immediate next steps for ArborPay infra & product teams: 

Summary: 
- Shortlist: redwood-7b-latency (8k), redwood-13b-optimized (16k), redwood-34b-window (32k) — use 34b only for reconciliation routes.
- Baseline tokens/hr (conservative): 1.1M. Daytime peak: ~4.8M tokens/hr. Burst spike planning: design for throttling/autoscale to cover 10–12M token/hr brief spikes.
- Initial Dedicated recommendation: 2 pods baseline + autoscale to 8; separate 34b pool of 2 pods behind a policy-driven routing rule.

Action items: 
- Connor: share MAP and SOW draft (I've attached MAP_ArborPay_v1.2.pdf).
- Ben: schedule a 30–45m infra sizing call to walk through XLSX assumptions with ArborPay infra (please include recommended autoscale rules and burst policy).
- Samir/Priya: confirm whether you want 16k or 32k for the default conversational endpoints (we recommended 16k to start, flip to 32k only if you see >60% sessions needing >12k context).

Proposed timeline:
- This week: Ben call with infra (we can do tomorrow 10am PT).
- Next week: Kickoff (1h) to finalize MAP and begin implementation sprint.

If that works I'll book both meetings and circulate invites + the XLSX.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
